articles.title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning

Abstract: When a fact becomes harder to elicit from a language model, has the model lost it, or has it merely become less accessible? Abstract: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. articles.title: BOLT: Multi-Bottleneck Bound-Guided Learning for Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling with Time Lags and Resource-Coupled Transport
articles.summary:
arXiv:2610.22433v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flexible job-shop scheduling becomes resource-coupled when a scarce vehicle fleet moves jobs between stations, because the schedule sets the transport waits. BOLT (bound-oriented learning for transport-coupled scheduling) builds a lower bound from chain, machine-capacity, and fleet-capacity relaxations. The bound equals the makespan at termination, so its per-step changes form a reward that sums to a constant minus the makespan. Because it never exceeds the attainable makespan, each candidate's bound increase is a proven rise of the makespan floor, which the policy reads as a price. Abstract: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. articles.title: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
articles.summary:
arXiv:2610.22460v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue. We argue this is a mistake. We make three claims. First, functional welfare already arises naturally and will become more robust as models acquire more coherent goals and personas.
